title: Agroforestry
claim: Integrating trees into farms and agricultural landscapes through agroforestry improves soil health and water management while supporting biodiversity that can approach the levels found in natural forests.
evidence_text: FAO's agroforestry programme describes agroforestry — the integration of trees on farms and in agricultural landscapes — as improving soil health and water management for land users while diversifying and sustaining production. FAO notes that agroforestry systems can support biodiversity levels approaching those of natural forests, making them a practical way to add structural habitat and water infiltration capacity within otherwise simplified cropland.
